speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; knowing your family history is very helpful. Given the swelling in your right knee, have you noticed any recent trauma, or does the pain worsen with activity? Also, have you experienced any locking, clicking, or instability in the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (systemic or oligoarticular) or possibly a genetic crystal arthropathy like CPPD given the family history and onset in a toddler, though trauma should still be ruled out. To narrow this down, I need to know if the swelling is constant or fluctuates, and if there are any rashes or fever. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, ESR, CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: Right knee X-ray.
